Name: Equal
comments: 12 quints reduced by 1/12 Pythagorean comma each.

Name: Just Intonation
comments: Sometimes known as Ptolemaic Chromatic, or Naturaly Harmonious (Barbour, Schugk), in the base "C" rotation works for C-major: perfect pitch for C-major, G-major, F-major, all other terribly out of tune.

Name: Pythagorean
comments: all quints pure except one, pythagorean comma placed between G#- D#, rotation shifts it anywhere you want. Thirds do not work well in this temperament.

Name: Grammateus (1518)
comments: Pythagorean comma split in two parts, applied between B-F# and Eb-Bb (base rotation C).

Name: Schlick (Vogel)
comments: reconstruction of Schlick (1511) by Harald Vogel, 7 quints reduced by ca. 1/5 of pythagorean comma. Two enlarged by the same.

Name: Meantone (-1/4)
comments: 8 pure thirds, quints -1/4 syntonic comma except one "wolf quint" placed between G#-D# in the base rotation "C". First described with certainty by Pietro Aaron (1523).

Name: Rameau (1726)
comments: one possible reconstruction. Variant of Meantone (4 pure thirds), Rameau suggests seven quints from Bb narrowed by 1/4 synt. comma, next quints should be made "purer" and the remaining two wide to match the quint circle.

Name: Ordinaire
comments: D'Alembert/Rousseau 1752/67 rendition of the French historical "Ordinaire" temperament. Four quints reduced by 1/4 Pythagorean comma, Four quints reduced by 1/12 and for quints enlarged by 1/12.

Name: Valotti (Tartini)
comments: Valotti's temperament as reported by G. Tartini, using Pythagorean comma fractions. Six quints reduced by 1/6 Pythagorean comma.

Name: Valotti (orig.)
comments: Valotti's historical temperament. 6 quints reduced by 1/6 syntonic comma, schisma placed on Bb-F.

Name: Trost (1677)
comments: Not to be confused with the organbuilder Trost, this is Johann Caspar. Early attempt at well-tempered, 8 quints reduced by max. 1/4 Pythagorean comma, 4 quints enlarged by the same amount.

Name: Werckmeister III
comments: four quints reduced by 1/4 Pythagorean comma. Andreas Werckmeister, Erweiterte und verbesserte Orgel-Probe (1698), I. was theoretical just intonation with sub-semitonia, II. was the 1/4 meantone (alte, falsche, unrichtige Temperatur).

Name: Werckmeister IV
comments: several quints reduced or augmented by 1/3 Pythagorean comma. Andreas Werckmeister, Erweiterte und verbesserte Orgel-Probe (1698), I. was theoretical just intonation with sub-semitonia, II. was the 1/4 meantone (alte, falsche or unrichtige Temperatur).

Name: Werckmeister V
comments: several quints reduced or augmented by 1/4 Pythagorean comma. Andreas Werckmeister, Erweiterte und verbesserte Orgel-Probe (1698), I. was theoretical just intonation with sub-semitonia, II. was the 1/4 meantone (alte, falsche or unrichtige Temperatur).

Name: Silbermann (-1/6s)
comments: reconstruction of G. Silbermann temperament, variant of 1/6 comma meantone. All quints narrowed by 1/6 syntonic comma, except one "wolf quint" Ab-Eb (in the default C rotation).

Name: Silbermann (-1/6p)
comments: reconstruction of G. Silbermann temperament, variant using fractions of the Pythagorean comma. All quints narrowed by 1/6 pythagorean comma, except one "wolf quint" Ab-Eb (in the default C rotation).

Name: Kirnberger I
comments: D-A lowered by a syntonic comma (terribly out of tune), and F#-C# reduced by a schisma. Kirnberger was a pupil of J. S. Bach.

Name: Kirnberger II
comments: Half syn. comma reduction applied to D-A and A-E, schisma to F#-C#. Easy to tune - most quints remain pure. This may be the reason for popularity of this awkward temperament. C major sounds rather out of tune. Kirnberger was a pupil of J. S. Bach.

Name: Kirnberger III
comments: quarter syn. comma reduction applied to C-G,G-C,D-A,A-E. Schism applied to F#-C#. Attempt to mitigate the C major chord. Kirnberger was a pupil of J. S. Bach.

Name: Bach (Kellner, 1977)
comments: modern reconstruction by Herbert Anton Kellner, "Eine Rekonstruktion der wohltemperierten Stimmung von Johann Sebastian Bach" 1977. Five quints narrowed by 1/5 Pythagorean comma.

Name: Neidhardt I Kleine Stadt
comments: Kleine Stadt 1732 (Tertiarum Circulus II), Dorf 1724, notation "I" from Barbour 1951.

Name: Neidhardt II Grosse Stadt 1732
comments: Grosse Stadt 1732 (Quintarum Circulus VIII), Kleine Stadt 1724, notation "II" from Barbour 1951.

Name: Neidhardt III Grosse Stadt 1724
comments: Grosse Stadt 1724, Altenburg Castle Original Organ Temperament, not reproduced in Neidhardt 1732, notation "III" from Barbour 1951.

Name: Neidhardt Hof (=Equal)
comments: Hof 1724+1732, = Equal, 1732 (Quintarum Circulus I)

Name: Neidhardt Dorf
comments: Dorf 1732, (Tertiarum Circulus I)

Name: Neidhardt 3rd Cycle III
comments: Another example from 1732 (Tertiarum Circulus III)

Name: Neidhardt 5th Cycle V
comments: Another example from 1732 (Quintarum Circulus X)

Name: Sorge (1758)
comments: Temperamentum inequale modernum. Several fifths reduced by 1/6 or 1/12 Pyth. comma. An attempt to modernize "old" Silbermann's temperament, G. A. Sorge, Zuverlaessige Anweisung, Claviere und Orgeln... (1758).

Name: Sorge (1744 I)
comments: four quints reduced by 1/4 Pyth. comma. Rest pure quints. G. A. Sorge, Anweisung zur Stimmung und Temperatur sowohl der Orgelwerke ... (1744).

Name: Sorge (1744 II)
comments: Quints reduced by 1/12 or 1/6 Pyth. comma. Three pure quints. G. A. Sorge, Anweisung zur Stimmung und Temperatur sowohl der Orgelwerke ... (1744).

Name: Sorge (1744 III)
comments: Quints reduced by 1/12 or 1/6 Pyth. comma. Four pure quints. G. A. Sorge, Anweisung zur Stimmung und Temperatur sowohl der Orgelwerke ... (1744).
